newsitem.title: UK: UK's Henderson expects success in EU border talks.
newsitem.headline: UK's Henderson expects success in EU border talks.

text.p: Britain will successfully negotiate with its European Union partners to keep control of its borders, Minister for Europe Doug Henderson said on Monday.

"We've indicated that getting control of our own borders is a priority and we are optimistic we will be able to achieve that over the next 24 hours," he told BBC radio from Amsterdam, where European Union leaders are meeting to ratify a new treaty, taking EU nations forward to a single currency.
On Monday, a stability pact deal was agreed, giving more emphasis to jobs and growth. But EU leaders continued to work through a blanket draft treaty to be written up for agreement on Tuesday.
Among other initiatives, it is expected to lift internal border controls across the continent.
Henderson said both border systems would be involved in the overall treaty. Ireland and Britain had different requirements because they were island nations, he said.
"What we've said is we want to see the British system of frontier control put into the treaty. That means it's a balanced agreement which is what we are seeking."
But that did not mean Britain would be excluded forever from the rump of a bloc which has dropped common borders.
"If at a later stage, we or the Irish wish to move to the same system or accept some of the system that the other countries have, then we must have the right to do that," he said.
"We would be hope to tie that up in the text either tonight or tomorrow morning. These are important issues. We think we will be successful," he said.
